name: Devs.ai
summary: Build and ship AI agents and apps across many models without engineering work.
best_for: teams that want to prototype and ship AI agents and apps across multiple models without engineering overhead, and that can absorb model usage metered on top of the per-seat fee
skip_if: you need SSO, access control lists or white-labelling without going through an Enterprise contract, or you need one predictable all-in bill rather than a seat fee plus metered usage
honest_knock: The seat price is the smaller half of the bill. Personal includes $10 of usage a month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat. The plan cards state the included amount without stating the rate you pay once it runs out, which is exactly the number you need to forecast a real workload. The free plan is a demo rather than a working tier: both builders are limited to "Core", and workflows, APIs and integrations are absent entirely, which is much of what would make the platform useful past a first agent. And for a product sold on IT governance, the governance controls are the ones you cannot buy with a card: SSO, access control lists and white-labelling sit on the Enterprise tier, behind a custom annual contract.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Personal, per seat · per seat per month billed annually ($18 billed monthly)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-11 and 2026-08-26, read in a live browser session on devs.ai/home/pricing with both billing toggles) Devs.ai does publish its pricing — on the marketing site at devs.ai/home/pricing, not at the app's /pricing route, which bounces you to a login screen. Free is $0 forever, but Agent Builder and App Builder appear there in "Core" rather than "Full" form, data upload is capped at 2 GB, and workflows, APIs and integrations are marked absent. Personal is $15 per seat / month billed annually or $18 billed monthly; Business is $30 per seat / month annually or $36 monthly; Enterprise is a custom annual contract. The seat fee is not the whole bill: Personal includes $10 of usage per month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat. Data upload runs 2 GB, 10 GB, 20 GB and custom across the four tiers. Team governance and collaboration start at Business, while SSO (SAML 2.0 only, per the SSO documentation), access control lists, custom connectors and white-labelling are Enterprise-only. Separately, Devs.ai told us by email on 5 August 2026 that organisations upgrading to a paid Personal or Business plan can earn up to $100 in usage credits for completing setup steps: starting a conversation, creating an agent, connecting an integration, deploying an app. The credits are shared org-wide and do not expire. Enterprise is excluded, and orgs already on a paid plan before July 2026 are not enrolled by default. That last paragraph is the vendor's own statement to us, not something we found published on the pricing page.

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested Devs.ai on the Free plan: one small support reply app built with the App Builder, used once with a made up email, and the cost shown in Analytics. Nothing was deployed or shared. The prompt was A simple tool for a small support team: paste a customer email, pick a tone, and get a short polite reply draft to copy. Build was pressed at about 17:26. The app Support Email Tone Reply Draft was ready after about 3.5 minutes: a page Support reply draft tool with a field Customer email or issue, a tone choice (Warm: Kind, reassuring, human), Clear, Generate, example chips and a Reply draft box with Copy. It picked up the AIBuilder house style and a dark mode by itself. A made up customer email about being charged twice for October and asking for a refund of one payment gave within about 10 seconds a fitting draft: an apology, a request for the account email and the dates or last four digits of the two charges, and no promise of a refund up front. The build model was GPT-5.5; the app assistant model shown in Analytics was Grok 4.6. The Deploy button was not used, so nothing was deployed or shared. Analytics after the test: Total Chats 2, Total Tokens 1.1M, Total Cost 1.01 USD (In 0.71, Out 0.30). The breakdown: the chat TypeScript Build Errors on GPT-5.5, 1 message, 1.1M tokens, 1.00 dollar; the app assistant on Grok 4.6, 3 messages, 5.8K tokens, 0.01 dollar. So building one small app cost 1.00 dollar, a tenth of the 10 dollars of usage included in Personal, and using the app cost 0.01 dollar. The rate beyond the included amount is not shown on the Upgrade page. Single sign on for IT teams is an Enterprise matter and was not tested. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The Upgrade page shows no rate for usage beyond the included amount, so the cost above 10 or 21 dollars a month is unknown.

sessions.what: We built one small app in Devs.ai's App Builder on the Free plan on 13 November 2026 and read the cost in its Analytics screen. The account is Daan's, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We deployed and shared nothing: the app sits in the account as a draft. We did not test checkout, support, export or cancellation.
findings: The App Builder asks 'What do you want to build?' with a model picker set to GPT-5.5, a Plan first option and templates such as CRM, Analytics Dashboard and HR Portal. The Free plan showed unlimited users and no card.

We typed one sentence: a tool for a small support team where you paste a customer email, pick a tone and get a short polite reply draft. After about three and a half minutes the app was ready, with an email field, a tone picker, a Generate button and a Copy button.

We pasted a made-up customer email about being charged twice. Within about ten seconds the app returned a polite draft that apologised, asked for the account email and the payment dates, and did not promise a refund up front.

Analytics, the vendor's own meter, showed $1.01 in total after the test: $1.00 for the build chat (1.1 million tokens, GPT-5.5) and $0.01 for the app's assistant (5.8K tokens, Grok 4.6). The upgrade page lists Personal at $15 per seat a month including $10 of usage, and Business at $30 including $21. We did not see a rate for usage above the included amount on that page. We did not check the meter against an independent source.
The upgrade page shows a yearly option labelled Save 16%. We did not open checkout, so tax, renewal terms and the payable total are unknown.
not_tested: Sign-up on a fresh account (the session began inside the App Builder)
What a build costs on Personal, and the rate above the included usage
SSO (Enterprise only), checkout, support, export, roles, downgrade and cancelling
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
